references.text: Jacob's sons took all their livestock, their children, and their women as captives, and plundered everything in the houses. An earlier example of taking women, children, and property as war spoils.

The law concerning war spoils: you shall take the women, children, livestock, and everything in the city as your spoil. This verse provides the legal background for the practice described in Num 31:9.
Rules for taking a woman captive in war. Explains how the Israelites were to treat female captives.
Moses gives further instructions regarding the captives from Midian, specifying who was to live and who was to be killed.
A detailed list of the spoils from Midian, including livestock and young women. Provides specific numbers for those taken captive.
The Lord grants Joshua permission to take spoil and livestock from Ai. A similar example of divine approval for taking war spoils.
David recovers the women and children who had been taken captive by the Amalekites. Illustrates the practice of taking women and children as captives in war.
